issues.failure_explanation: With the stated signed-distance and outward-normal conventions, the boundary point is x-r(x)n(x), not x+r(x)n(x). For an exterior point of a ball, the printed map moves farther outside. Consequently, both extension formulas evaluate data outside their declared domains: g is boundary data, and the exterior branch for f still evaluates f outside Omega. This error occurs in the actual data-evaluation construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the evaluation point by x-r(x) nbar(x) in both extension formulas wherever the nearest-point projection is defined. Global admissibility requires the separate repair in ISSUE-002.
issues.overall_effect: The prescribed extensions, and therefore the nonhomogeneous right-hand sides using them, are not defined for general boundary and interior data.
issues.title: The data-extension map does not project onto the boundary
issues.why_classification: Correcting the evaluation map is a local algorithmic repair determined by the stated normal-coordinate identity; it does not require changing the diffusion formulations or their coercivity arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We smoothly extend both function so that they are constant in the normal direction to the original boundary, $\partial\domain{}$
This extension is only required in a small neighbourhood around the boundary.

issues.failure_explanation: Even after correcting the projection sign, normal projection is only single-valued in a suitable tubular neighborhood, not throughout a general B. For example, on the unit disk, smooth boundary data g(y)=y_1 have normal-constant extension gbar(x)=x_1/|x|, which is not continuous at the center and is not in H1 in two dimensions. The exact tanh profile has 0<phi<1 everywhere at finite distance, so the claim that only neighborhood values are needed does not make the global formulas or the H1 trial-space lifting well-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict normal extension to a tubular neighborhood with unique projection, state the required boundary/data regularity, and construct an H1-compatible continuation away from that neighborhood using a cutoff or another extension.
issues.overall_effect: The paper has not constructed globally admissible data for its stated trial spaces and diffuse integrals, even for some smooth domains and smooth boundary data.
issues.title: Global smooth normal extensions are not available as asserted
issues.why_classification: A contained extension construction and geometric hypotheses are needed; changing the projection sign alone cannot resolve this defect.

issues.failure_explanation: The computed diagonal contains |grad(phi u)|^2, whereas the asserted norm contains phi|grad u|^2. These are not the DDM1 energy with a different epsilon exponent. Positivity of the former expression does not by itself supply the claimed norm inequality; a comparison controlling the product-rule cross term and the different gradient weight is missing.

failure_location.quote: This is identical, up to epsilon scalling, to DDM1,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For fixed epsilon on a bounded computational domain, use phi grad u=grad(phi u)-u grad phi, the stated phase-field derivative bound, and inf_B phi>0 to prove the missing comparison. Explicitly allow the resulting constant to depend on epsilon.
issues.overall_effect: The stated SBM norm-coercivity estimate, and the subsequent proof invoking it for advection, are not established by the supplied argument.
issues.title: SBM coercivity is inferred in the wrong norm
issues.why_classification: A short Young-inequality comparison repairs the stated fixed-epsilon claim; no epsilon-uniform coercivity constant was promised.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Multiplying by $\phi$
and substituting \cref{eq:mixed0-strong1} gives a new method,

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying the preceding equation by phi produces D epsilon^(-2) phi(1-phi)(u-g), not D epsilon^(-2)(1-phi)^2(u-g). The latter coefficient is retained in the method and its proof, so this is an unacknowledged change of the constructed equation rather than an isolated display error. In particular, the two coefficients have different exterior behavior.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert an explicit modeling step replacing phi(1-phi) by (1-phi)^2 to control the exterior, and distinguish that modified method from the equation obtained solely by multiplication and substitution.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed Mixed0 equation does not follow from the claimed elimination of the mixed system. Its separate coercivity proof for the chosen squared penalty remains applicable.
issues.title: Mixed0 elimination changes the penalty coefficient
issues.why_classification: The already-analyzed method can be retained by making the additional penalty choice explicit; no new coercivity argument or advertised convergence theorem must be replaced.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $D := D(x) \geq d > 0$ is a scalar function.
Also, we take the non-constant scalar diffusion coefficient,

issues.failure_explanation: The first term of l(v) needs the same factor D as the corresponding bilinear diffusion term. The omission is repeated in the advection version. For constant D different from 1, f=0, and constant data g=C, the intended diffuse strong equation admits u=C, but the printed weak method leaves residual (D-1)C times the integral of grad(phi) dot [grad(phi v)+v grad(phi)], which is generally nonzero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore D in the first boundary-data term of both meth:mixed0 and meth:mixed0adv, and ensure the reported computations correspond to that corrected formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The printed Mixed0 and Mixed0-advection procedures are inconsistent with their stated diffuse equations for non-unit diffusivity and nonzero data. Coercivity of their bilinear forms does not resolve the incorrect forcing.
issues.title: Mixed0 omits diffusivity from its boundary forcing
issues.why_classification: The intended coefficient is already determined by the strong equation. Restoring it is local and leaves all bilinear forms, norms, and coercivity arguments unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing q=b dot grad(phi), the boundary contribution is phi(-q+q^+)=-phi q^-, not phi|q|/2. For q>0 the actual contribution is zero while the claimed expression is positive. The proof imports the one-half decomposition from the single-phi advection calculation even though differentiating phi squared produces a factor two.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the faulty decomposition by -phi[b dot grad(phi)]^- >= 0 and complete the proof with the mass term.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted intermediate energy identity is false, independently of the SBM diffusion-norm gap. The desired nonnegativity conclusion nevertheless remains available.
issues.title: SBM advection proof introduces an incorrect factor one-half
issues.why_classification: A local replacement identity proves exactly the required nonnegativity without changing the scheme or theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The remaining mass/divergence coefficient is phi m-phi^2 div(b)/2 = phi^2(m-div(b)/2)+phi(1-phi)m. The last term cannot be discarded unless m is nonnegative. The stated condition allows m<0. For example, in one dimension take m=-M and b(x)=-2M(x-a) near the right boundary x=a of an interval. Then m-b'/2=0, and on an interior-supported test function near that boundary b phi'<0. The advection-plus-mass energy is therefore -M integral phi(1-phi)u^2, which defeats the fixed diffusion energy for sufficiently large M.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add m>=0 to this theorem and its advertised scope, and retain the nonnegative remainder phi(1-phi)m in the proof; alternatively impose the directly sufficient weighted mass/divergence condition.
issues.overall_effect: Mixed1 with advection is not necessarily coercive under the paper's stated data condition, even for smooth coefficients.
issues.title: Mixed1 advection needs an additional mass-sign hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained, but it substantively narrows the allowed reaction/advection data rather than merely correcting algebra.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the $H^1$ errors \MixedZ{} preforms the best,

issues.failure_explanation: For the mixed methods, sigma_h is not grad(u_h). For Mixed0, sigma_h=grad(u_h)+(u_h-g)grad(phi)/phi. Thus the reported quantity measures scalar-plus-recovered-flux error, not the H1 error of u_h. No estimate is supplied that transfers its convergence rate or superiority to the actual gradient error; the correction can scale like epsilon^(-1) in the interface.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Report recovered-flux error separately and restrict the associated conclusions to that quantity. To retain H1 claims, compute grad(u_h)-based errors for every method or prove a suitable reconstruction estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The H1 comparisons between mixed and non-mixed methods, including the Taylor-Green and appendix conclusions, do not establish the claimed H1 accuracy advantage of the computed scalar or velocity field.
issues.title: Recovered-flux errors are reported as H1 solution errors
issues.why_classification: Relabeling preserves useful flux-accuracy evidence, but the asserted H1 convergence comparison must be withdrawn or supported by additional analysis or measurements.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We smoothly extend both function so that they are constant in the normal direction to the original boundary, $\partial\domain{}$

issues.failure_explanation: The searchlight boundary data have jump discontinuities along the smooth two-dimensional boundary. Such a step trace is not in H^(1/2), so it has no H1 lifting with that trace. Its normal-constant extension also jumps across curves and is not H1. Consequently, the stated construction U=H1_0(B)+g is not an admissible H1 trial space for this benchmark. An unstated finite-element interpolation or regularization is not the same input problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the tested methods, specify an independent H1 lifting for the outer boundary and use the discontinuous diffuse data only in the L2 right-hand-side terms, with a stated discretization of the jumps; alternatively introduce and document a boundary-data regularization.
issues.overall_effect: The searchlight application is not defined by the paper's stated trial-space and smooth-extension construction, although a different low-regularity diffuse formulation could be defined.
issues.title: Searchlight data do not admit the required H1 lifting
issues.why_classification: A genuine adjustment of the lifting/data treatment is required. This is a contained construction, but it is not a notational correction to the existing H1 setup.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: this figure shows an approximation of the expected solution given $D=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The printed advection coefficient is b=(x_1,-x_0), a clockwise rotation. On the upper end-cap highlighted green, it points out of the arc; the lower end-cap is the inflow. For example, at the middle of the upper cap, the source's geometry gives b dot n=1/2>0. The nonnegative searchlight band is prescribed on this outflow, whereas the incoming data are -0.5. The depicted band transported through the arc therefore corresponds to the opposite velocity, not to the stated vanishing-diffusion problem.

failure_location.quote:
the green part of the boundary shows the inflow
and black is characteristic or outflow.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the advection sign to match the depicted upper inflow, or change the prescribed illuminated boundary and expected solution to match clockwise transport; then verify the reported experiment against the consistently specified problem.
issues.overall_effect: The inflow classification, expected searchlight solution, and convergence interpretation of that benchmark are inconsistent with its printed PDE.
issues.title: The searchlight inflow and expected solution use the opposite rotation
issues.why_classification: The repair changes a benchmark's transport problem and requires revalidation of its interpretation, but no new global numerical-method architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated outward normal derivative, integration by parts gives integral D grad(p) dot grad(q)=integral f q+integral_boundary D p_N q. The diffuse equation should therefore have -D p_N|grad(phi)| on its left-hand side. The printed term instead corresponds to prescribing negative conormal flux -p_N, not the stated normal derivative p_N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the boundary term by -D p_N|grad(phi)|, or consistently redefine the boundary datum and its sign throughout the model.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised nonhomogeneous Neumann construction imposes the wrong boundary flux. The homogeneous pressure-correction examples are unaffected because p_N=0 there.
issues.title: The diffuse Neumann term uses the wrong flux convention
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the boundary-forcing coefficient restores the weak formulation, and all explicitly used homogeneous-Neumann cases remain unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
During the experiments we measure three quantities of interest \cite{Kilian2002,John2002}:
drag coefficient, $c_d(t)$,
lift coefficient, $c_l(t)$,
Here $r(x)$ is the signed distance function for the original domain;

issues.failure_explanation: For the defined fluid domain, partial Omega includes the inlet, outlet, and channel walls as well as the cylinder. Total traction on that boundary is not the cylinder drag/lift functional. Likewise, the phase field defined from distance to the whole physical boundary does not automatically provide a cylinder-only surface delta. Merely keeping the outer boundary fitted does not justify replacing a cylinder-surface integral by the displayed whole-boundary integral.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the force surface explicitly as the cylinder boundary and use a cylinder-localized phase-field gradient or a cutoff that excludes all outer-boundary contributions. Check the coefficient measurements with that estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The source does not correctly define the cylinder-force quantities used in its reference comparisons; additional boundary tractions may be included in the printed estimator.
issues.title: The cylinder-force estimator integrates the whole fluid boundary
issues.why_classification: A localized measurement construction and verification of the benchmark coefficients are needed, although the underlying flow solver need not be redesigned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To make this method coercive, so we add the term
Note, we do not have to add any special treatment for the inflow boundary,

issues.failure_explanation: The proved Mixed0 diffusion formulation explicitly contains the additional D|grad(phi)|^2(u-g)/4 stabilization, and its coercivity proof uses that term to complete the square. What is established without a further stabilizer is only the advection augmentation. The unqualified conclusion claims a stronger stabilization-free property than the analysis supplies.

failure_location.quote:
Notably, \MixedZ{} method was the only method proven to be
coercive without an additional stabilisation term,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to the absence of additional advection/inflow stabilization and explicitly retain the diffusion stabilization required by the proved method.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion misstates the mathematical advantage established for Mixed0; it does not prove coercivity of the unstabilized diffusion construction.
issues.title: The conclusion overstates stabilization-free coercivity of Mixed0
issues.why_classification: This withdraws a substantive but limited unqualified guarantee while preserving the established stabilized method and its advection-specific advantage.
